title: Your headache can be more sinister if you have these revealing symptoms … after the Mellencamp Diagnostic shock
text:
Experts have revealed the revealing signs that their headache could be something more pernicious after the diagnosis of Teddi Mellencamp’s brain tumor.
The real Housewives star of Beverly Hills revealed this week that she has several masses in her brain after several weeks of “severe and weakening headaches.”
Headaches are one of the most common ailments in the United States, which affect 96 percent of Americans at some point in their lives, and are generally harmless.
But in rare cases, a seemingly harmless headache can be the first sign of a deadly tumor.
If the pain hits early in the morning, it could be a sign that a tumor was pressing on the skull during sleep.
Brain tumors also cause headaches that worsen when coughing and sneezing, since the sensation irritates the tissue and surrounding blood vessels.
And vomiting can be a ‘red flag’ due to the increase in brain pressure that triggers nausea.
Having a history of melanoma can also increase the risk, since up to 70 percent of patients with advanced melanoma develop brain tumors.
Teddi Mellencamp, 43, revealed a devastating health update on Wednesday and shared “multiple tumors” in his brain, which resulted in his need for emergency surgery; Seen in 2024 in Los Angeles

Almost 100,000 Americans are diagnosed with brain tumors every year, and approximately one and four of these cause cancer.
According to the American Cancer Society, around 18,000 Americans die of brain tumors or spinal cord every year.
Headaches tend to be the most common sign of a brain tumor, although seizures, the difficulty in speaking, personality changes, weakness, numbness, loss of balance, audition and changes in vision also They are common.
It means that your headache could be somewhat more serious The headaches that begin as soon as you wake up, are accompanied by nausea or vomiting, worsen with cough or sneezing, or suddenly begin later in life it could be a sign of a brain tumor, experts have warned.
The general risk, however, is low.
However, the risk of developing a brain tumor is one percent.
In a Instagram reos Published last year, the doctor of the Pediatric Emergency Room, Dr. Meghan Martin, said the headaches early in a morning as a sign of ‘red flag’ brain tumor.
She said: “Brain tumors can cause headaches, but the raffle is the time of headache.”
Brain tumors press the surrounding cells and cause pressure in the brain.
Going to bed, how to sleep, makes the tumor more directly press on these cells and tissues, which makes pressure increase.
This high pressure can also make people with brain tumors wake up in the middle of the night.
Dr. Martin also said that the increase in the pressure of brain tumors can also stimulate parts of the encephalic trunk responsible for vomiting, so a headache that comes with nausea and vomiting is another red flag.
The pain that worsens of sensations such as cough and sneezing could also indicate a brain tumor because the cough or sneezing further irritates the tissues against which a tumor is pressed.
About 96 percent of Americans suffer at least a headache at some point in their lives, but the risk of developing a brain tumor is less than one percent
In Recent Video of Tiktok The Michigan -based neurologist, Dr. Baibing Chen, warned that the development of the head suddenly after 50 could be a sign of a brain tumor.
The probability of developing more common head and migraine disorders decreases with age due to changes in hormone production that make the brain more sensitive to pain, such as estrogen.
The development of headaches in the elderly, such as after menopause, could be a sign that they are caused by conditions such as a brain tumor.
Headaches around the forehead and center of the face can also indicate a tumor in the pituitary gland, which controls the production of hormones.
Pituitary tumors are one of the most common types of cancerous mass, which accumulates for one in 10 brain tumors.
A family history of brain cancer can also increase risk, although most tumors are not led.
Dr. Martin said that people with these symptoms should see a doctor for a computerized tomography or magnetic resonance to rule out the possibility of a brain tumor.
